Not every mistake is the same.

A BLUNDER is a serious mistake.
A SLIP-UP is a small accidental mistake.
An OVERSIGHT happens when you forget or fail to notice something.
A TYPO is a typing or printing mistake.
A MISUNDERSTANDING is when someone understands something incorrectly.

Using the right word makes your English sound more natural and precise. 💬

Hello Members! 👋
You’re building real strength in your communication — calm, clear, and confident.
Today’s lesson will help you respond when someone says “You always…” or “You never…” during an argument. ✨
🌟 TODAY’S CONTENT: HANDLING “YOU ALWAYS / YOU NEVER” STATEMENTS
🔹 Don’t React to the Exaggeration
These phrases are emotional, not factual.
Stay calm and say
That may feel that way to you.
I don’t think it’s always the case.
Let’s look at this more specifically.
Calm response reduces intensity.
🔹 Bring It Back to Facts
Shift from generalisation to reality.
Say
Can we talk about this specific situation?
Let’s focus on what happened this time.
What exactly are you referring to?
Specifics bring clarity.
🔹 Avoid Counter-Attacks
Don’t respond with
You always do this too!
Instead say
Let’s keep this focused.
I’d like to understand the actual issue.
Stay mature.
🔹 Acknowledge the Emotion
Sometimes they just want to be heard.
Say
I understand you’re upset.
I can see this is bothering you.
I hear what you’re saying.
Validation calms the moment.
🔹 Clarify Your Side
Respond with balance.
Say
From my side, it’s not like that.
Here’s what actually happened…
Let me explain my perspective.
Facts over emotion.
🔹 Close Calmly
End without escalation.
Say
Let’s work through this calmly.
I’d like us to resolve this.
Let’s move forward from here.
🌈 Why this matters
Handling exaggeration well
• prevents arguments from escalating
• builds emotional intelligence
• strengthens calm communication
• protects your confidence
🎯 Mini task
Practise saying this aloud once:
“Let’s focus on this specific situation.”
Say it calmly and clearly.
That’s confident communication 💫
